final_answer_text:
## Summary

**Scenario:** `scenario-043cffd4d852512e` — 30 s duration, node backend, `vehicle-b-rudder` on `coupled6` plant, single waypoint mission to (north=20 m, east=0 m).

**Run:** `run-8a50f88f-bfd9-42eb-a5bb-345bec84e9a6` — completed successfully, reached the waypoint in **7.7 s** (77 steps at 0.1 s timestep), well inside the 30 s allotted duration.

**Metrics:**
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Propulsion energy | 2.976 J |
| Total sensor cost | 41.195 J |
| Total energy (propulsion + sensors) | 44.171 J |
| Movement cost | 2.976 J |

Note the run's own `completion_time_s`/`elapsed_s` (7.7 s) reflects the time to reach the single waypoint, not the full 30 s window you configured — the simulation ended early once the goal was hit rather than running out the clock.

**Evidentiary status — important caveat:** `vehicle-b-rudder` carries validation status **`model-structure-trajectory-scored-fail`**. Per the preset's own claim: its MMG-style simulator was scored against six measured MARIN KVLCC2 trajectories (with real rudder/RPM inputs), and the literature-coefficient parameterization **failed** the precommitted trajectory/IMO tolerances. Critically, **no evidence validates the USV-scale coefficients actually used for Vehicle B** — the validation exercise was done at ship scale, not at this vehicle's scale.

**Bottom line:** The run executed and produced numbers, but those numbers should be treated as **illustrative/exploratory only, not validated predictions** of real-world behavior. Any energy, trajectory, or timing conclusions drawn from this run should be caveated accordingly — this vehicle model has a documented validation failure and an unvalidated parameterization gap.
